title.text: Continuing Education Requirements for Sunshine Day Care Employees

textContent.text: Sunshine Day Care follows all regulations set forth by the state's Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS) regarding continuing education requirements for day care employees.

All Sunshine Day Care employees in supervisory or direct care roles are required to complete 15 hours of in-service training every year. New employees must begin their continuing education courses within 60 days of hire.

Sunshine Day Care closes for one day each quarter to provide five hours of in-service staff training. Individual staff members must complete additional coursework as needed to fulfill their requirements. Credit hours must be approved by a supervisor and documentation should be uploaded to the Reliant portal to meet state mandates.

OCFS provides free online course modules that employees can complete at their own pace. Staff may also attend in-person, accredited workshops or enroll in hybrid or blended-learning classes. Any modality is acceptable as long as coursework falls under one of the following domains:

elements.text: Childhood behavioral development
Nutrition for infants and young children
Daycare program management
Safety and security in child care
Records and business documentation

textContent.text: Employees must complete coursework in at least three of these five domains each year. Hours earned in excess of the annual requirement are credited to your requirements for the following year. Employees may use Reliant to check their current credit hours. Please contact your supervisor if you believe Reliant does not accurately reflect your completed coursework.

title.text: Food for the People Volunteer Policy

textContent.text: For thirty years, Food for the People has relied on the generosity of community volunteers to support its regional food and gardening programs. The following policy helps ensure that Food for the People effectively uses volunteer services while remaining compliant with federal labor laws.

lines.text: Food for the People requires an application and interview for potential volunteers. Program leaders should clearly define volunteer duties so that the best applicants can be matched to available projects. Interviewers should carefully consider each individual's interests and skills, taking care to match prospective volunteers to projects that will interest them. Once a screened applicant has been matched with a program, his or her information should be shared with the team lead for that program. The lead will handle next steps in communication and training. We have found that this process has greatly increased volunteer satisfaction and retention over the years.

textContent.text: Volunteers cannot perform any duties that fall under the job description of a paid Food for the People employee. Relatedly, employees should not volunteer to perform tasks outside of their primary directive during work hours, though they may volunteer in other capacities after hours and on weekends.

lines.text: Food for the People cannot compensate volunteers for their time. Prohibited compensation includes monetary payments, exchange of services, gifts of substantial value, or other significant perks. For example, it would be inappropriate for Food for the People to provide food for a volunteer's personal event, or to grant a volunteer use of organization-owned computer software for a personal project.

textContent.text: Food for the People can provide refreshments to volunteers as they work. However, meals and other forms of appreciation cannot be dependent on volunteers donating a certain number of hours. Additionally, any provisions should not be significant or frequent; rather, they should remain nominal. Elaborate or expensive meals could appear to be an improper method of compensating volunteers for their service.

title.text: Digital Records Policy

textContent.text: The university is required to retain documents that may be needed for future legal proceedings. Digital records are governed by the same university rules that cover paper records. Therefore, any digital record that is necessary to meet the legal, fiscal, or administrative needs of the university must be secured by one or more of the following backup procedures:

elements.text: A paper copy of the digital record must be printed and filed with the Collegiate Archivist.
A copy of the digital record must be stored on the university's secure shared network.

textContent.text: The university considers emails to be a special category of digital record, so there is a separate procedure for how to handle them. The content of email messages will determine whether or not they need to be preserved as digital records. Emails should be preserved if they meet one or more of the following criteria:

elements.text: They prove a business-related event or activity did or did not occur.
They demonstrate a transaction for goods or services.
They communicate university policy, program, or procedural directives.

textContent.text: Emails that do not meet any of the above criteria are considered personal and may be freely deleted from your computer at any time. Emails that do meet any of the criteria are subject to the same retention periods as paper records and must be stored in both of the following ways:

elements.text: A paper copy of the email, including all header information, must be printed and stored in a secured location in your home or office.
A copy of the email and any attachments must be saved in a digital format, such as a PDF, and stored on the university's secure shared network.

title.text: Cleaning and Sanitizing Dishes at Stranger Wings

textContent.text: Stranger Wings is committed to following all restaurant safety guidelines issued by the Hawkins Department of Public Health. As such, kitchen staff at Stranger Wings are expected to comply with the guidelines below for cleaning dishes.

The kitchen's conveyor washer should be used for all glassware and porcelain bakeware. The industrial dishwashing machine should be used to clean and sanitize all dishes, utensils, and small pots and pans. Manual dishwashing is to be performed when cleaning large cookware and in the event that the dishwashing machine is unavailable.

Manual dishwashing should proceed in a three-step process: wash, rinse, and sanitize. This process must be completed in the three-compartment sink in the kitchen. In the first compartment, wash dishes with detergent and clean water at or above 110°F. After washing is completed, use the second compartment to rinse dishes with clean water. Finally, use the third compartment to immerse the dishes for at least 30 seconds in a solution of Hopper Magic and water that is at a temperature of 130°F or above. To figure out how much water and Hopper Magic is needed for dishes, please consult the manufacturer's label on the back of the bottle.

Please make sure that cleaning and sanitizing are done properly. Correct washing procedures can help prevent the spread of pathogens in the kitchen. Any outbreak could turn the restaurant upside down, affecting the health of our guests and the reputation of our restaurant.

title.text: SSE Travel Planning and Reimbursement

textContent.text: Speedy Sports and Entertainment agents are renowned for the personal attention they provide our athletes, actors, and other clients. Because travel is an integral part of the agent role, we have developed the following policies to ensure ease of travel planning and efficiency of post-travel reimbursement.

Jetsetters is our exclusive provider for travel and lodging. Their single-point service streamlines travel logistics and also provides real-time support for Speedy agents when they are on the road. Jetsetters customer service will present several itinerary options for each new lodging and travel request; Speedy employees are encouraged to choose the best rate whenever possible.

All reimbursement claims for Speedy agents are handled through the QuikPay portal. For more information on submitting through QuikPay, please consult the 'Reimbursement of Work-Related Expenses' section in Speedy's online employee handbook.

Travel expenses are covered under a per diem. This means that employees receive a flat, daily reimbursement rate which is set by region, adjusted annually for inflation, and designed to cover all meals and major travel-related costs. Employees may elect to submit an itemized expense report for the exact costs of other work-related expenses and incidentals accrued beyond the per diem. Examples of reimbursable incidentals include tips for waiters and hotel staff and bus or subway fare.

Employees choosing to be reimbursed for itemized expenses should maintain careful records and retain all receipts. Receipts are also required for all expenses over $25. If receipts are missing, or employees cannot otherwise provide exact details for their purchases, managerial review and approval of the expense report will be required. This will likely result in administrative delays and may lead to a reimbursement request being denied.
Managers and executive agents using Speedy company credit cards must retain receipts for all purchases, regardless of the amount, and submit them monthly to the Speedy finance department.

In order to receive reimbursement for ticket and event-related expenses, Speedy agents should only attend events where they will have direct contact with potential clients. A potential client is defined as a high-net-worth individual actively seeking representation. Plans to attend ticketed events to see potential clients must be pre-approved by a manager in order to qualify for reimbursement.

textContent.text: The skill and care that Mom and Pop's staff bring to the pottery glazing and firing process create high-quality finished pieces that our customers have come to expect and appreciate. This document presents the specific steps staff must follow to ensure that all finalized pottery projects are of high quality. All pieces need to be ready for customer pickup or shipping within ten days of any given pottery session.

Glazing is a critical process that requires attention to detail and proper handling of customer pieces. First, mix the appropriate glaze for the pieces to be fired. We use only standard clear glaze on children's pieces. Adult customers can choose between the clear glaze and a range of tinted glazes.

Before dipping any pieces, stir the glaze to remix settled particles. Remember to also check the glaze's viscosity. If the glaze is too thick, add water little by little until it looks like heavy cream when stirred.

Dip each piece in glaze for three to five seconds. To avoid possible breakage during glazing, never hold pottery by a small, fragile section, such as a handle on a mug or a horn on a unicorn. Pottery can quickly become heavy as it soaks up glaze.

Since melting glaze can fuse pieces to other surfaces, pieces should never touch one another or the sides of the kiln. Allowing enough room between pieces is of paramount importance, but we also want to maximize the number of pieces included in any firing session. When carefully placed, at least fifty medium-sized pieces of pottery can be safely loaded for a single firing. Avoid firing a partially loaded kiln whenever possible; firing pieces from multiple sessions at once is a best practice, especially when doing so ensures a full kiln.
Once pieces are properly glazed and loaded in the kiln, the firing process can begin. After closing the kiln, set it to the appropriate temperature.

(Examples: external hard drive larger than one terabyte needed for product photo shoot with Cheshire Cat and Co.; additional hi-res monitor needed for White Rabbit photo retouching, etc.). These devices will allow us to be more precise in color matching and achieving branding consistency. title.text: Avoiding Conflicts of Interest at Tempest Video Games

textContent.text: Employees of Tempest Video Games naturally have personal interests and connections outside of the workplace. Occasionally, it is necessary to evaluate these personal connections from a business standpoint. Tempest's requirement for reporting potential conflicts of interest in hiring and personnel decisions is designed to ensure that the company is hiring, retaining, and promoting the best people for the job.

lines.text: A conflict of interest arises when the relationships of a Tempest Video Game employee outside the company have the ability to impact professional responsibilities at work. Showing any favoritism in recruiting, hiring, and/or promotion violates company policy. The following relationships will be considered conflicts of interest in HR and hiring decisions:

elements.text: spouses
children
siblings
parents

textContent.text: Other relationships besides those outlined above might constitute a conflict of interest; employees should use their best judgment to determine if a potential conflict exists in such situations.

lines.text: To ensure that personnel decisions are not compromised by any conflicting interests, Tempest requires employees to disclose all known and potential conflicts. Proper disclosure occurs in two steps: first, an employee should discuss any potential conflict with his or her manager, who will help determine if a conflict actually exists and needs to be disclosed; second, in the instance of an actual conflict, an employee must file official disclosure paperwork with HR.

textContent.text: If Human Resources confirms that an employee has a conflict of interest in relation to another person, that employee will be asked to refrain from any decision-making process that affects the hiring, promotion, retention, or reclassification of the individual in question. An employee's recusal is not a negative reflection on their judgment or character. Rather, it ensures that best personnel management practices are followed. Recusal is the most effective way to eliminate even the appearance of impropriety.
